sections.h2: How can a Kissimmee homeowner sell in a hurry?
sections.html:
Owners in Kissimmee usually choose among a cash sale, an agent listing and a do-it-yourself sale. Cash finishes soonest, as no bank is involved and the closing date becomes a point you negotiate instead of a lender's schedule.

Listing shows the house to more shoppers and may bring a stronger price, though you accept open houses, repair requests after the inspection and the chance that a buyer's loan collapses late. If the property is vacant, the roof is worn, tenants are difficult or an estate needs closing out, certainty can be worth more than top dollar. When the house is in good shape and time is on your side, request a listing opinion as well and compare the two figures.

  • Put each offer in writing, with the closing day stated.
  • Learn who pays for the title policy and the deed tax.
  • Request proof of funds when the offer is all cash.

Kissimmee began as Allendale, a small trading post on the north shore of Lake Tohopekaliga, and it is now the Osceola County seat. In 1881 a Philadelphia saw manufacturer, Hamilton Disston, contracted to drain the surrounding land and deepen the Kissimmee River after buying four million acres for $1 million. Growth came in bursts. After Walt Disney World opened in 1971, the city went from 7,500 residents to 15,000 by 1980 and then to 30,000 by 1990. Retirees arrived in the 1950s, and an airport built in the 1940s lifted the population by 38 percent.

The result is a mix of ages on one street. A house from the 1950s ages differently from one built in the 1990s, so write down your build year, roof age and the date of the last wiring and plumbing work before offers arrive.

Kissimmee's code enforcement division handles over 5,000 cases a year. The city holds the property owner answerable even when a tenant caused the problem, so settle anything open before a buyer looks.

Typical violations: grass taller than 12 inches on an improved lot, vegetation above 18 inches on an unimproved lot, junk and trash, inoperable vehicles outside a garage, and cars on the lawn past two spaces beside the driveway. Cases left unresolved can reach the special magistrate, who sits in public on the second Monday of each month. When the city performs the corrective work, you receive the bill, and a lien may be recorded if it goes unpaid.

Work cannot begin until a building permit is issued and displayed so it can be seen from the road. If you began a repair, finish it or close out the permit. Anyone renting a short-term dwelling in the city needs a business tax receipt from both Osceola County and the city, renewed each year by September 30, so a vacation rental house should have that paperwork current.

A residential pool needs a barrier at least 48 inches tall with no gaps a small child could squeeze through, and address numbers must be at least three inches high. Both are quick fixes worth doing before photographs.

  • Mow and clear debris.
  • Move inoperable vehicles into a garage.
  • Close out open permits.
  • Pull your business tax receipts if the house is rented short term.

sections.h2: How Osceola County bills and collects property tax
sections.html:
Osceola's tax collector opens collection each November 1, with the gross figure due the following March 31.

Early-payment discounts, Osceola tax collector
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone, gross amount

Delinquency starts April 1, when 3 percent is added to the gross amount. With an escrowed loan, the lender requests the bill and you get a copy.

Certificates are sold online by June 1. A certificate is a first-priority lien, not a sale of the land. If one stays unredeemed for two years, the holder may begin a tax deed application, and the clerk then lists the parcel for an online auction. Redeeming on or after June 1 adds a $6.25 fee to the payoff. Value and homestead filings come from the county property appraiser's office, 2505 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Highway in Kissimmee.

sections.h2: What happens to your homestead and tax savings when you sell?
sections.html:
The exemption belongs to the owner rather than the house, so a sale ends it at that address.

Florida's homestead exemption removes up to $50,000 of value. The first $25,000 applies to all taxing bodies and the second slice to non-school taxes only. Yearly assessment growth is capped at the smaller of 3 percent or inflation under Save Our Homes, which explains why a long-held house sits well below market. January 1 after the sale starts a fresh assessment at full just value.

If you buy again in Florida, portability can move part of the capped difference to the new home. You have three years, counted from January 1 of the year you gave up the old homestead, and you file by March 1.

sections.h2: The deed, who signs it, and tenants
sections.html:
Deed tax here is the statewide 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, due to the clerk at recording.

The state treats every party to the deed as liable, which leaves the question of who pays to a private arrangement between buyer and seller. The clerk bills recording by the page, beginning at $5.00. Two witnesses are required, and remote video witnessing is allowed.

Tenants in place bring notice clocks: a month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days' written notice, and a nonpayment notice runs 3 days with weekends and court holidays left out. If a foreclosure is pending, the clerk's auction is set 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff allows longer, so a sale ahead of that date is what protects your equity.

Once the contract is signed, the closing agent starts title work, requests a payoff letter from every lender and reviews the tax bill along with any open code or permit matters. The deed is prepared, signed before two witnesses and recorded by the clerk. Tax still unpaid for the year is divided between you and the buyer.

A cash buyer has no loan appraisal to wait on, so the schedule rests on title and recording. Get the timeline in writing before agreeing to a closing day, and keep your code enforcement and permit records close by in case the buyer's agent asks. If the house is a short-term rental, add the business tax receipts, and if it has tenants, add each lease and the notice dates.

faqs.q: Where is the Osceola County property appraiser's office?
faqs.a: Go to 2505 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Highway in Kissimmee. Record searches, sales transactions and map search are offered, and homestead filings are due there by March 1.

faqs.q: Does Kissimmee code enforcement follow a house after a sale?
faqs.a: Unresolved cases and recorded liens can remain on the parcel. Contact the city's code enforcement division for your address's status. A lien can be filed if the city performs work and the bill goes unpaid.

faqs.q: Does renting the house short term need city paperwork?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone renting a short-term dwelling within city limits needs a business tax receipt from both Osceola County and the city, renewed each year by September 30. The building division can tell you what fits your address.

faqs.q: When does an Osceola tax certificate turn into a tax deed risk?
faqs.a: Two years after April 1 of the sale year, an unredeemed certificate's holder can apply. The clerk then sets an online auction. Paying off the certificate through the tax collector first ends it.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Yes, once someone holds authority to sign. Summary administration exists for small or older estates, and creditor claims end on a fixed schedule. A probate attorney can say which path fits.
